context_title: Your task is to take the provided technical description and rewrite it as a single, comprehensive prompt. Write it as if you were about to build the entire system from scratch: describe step by step, from beginning to end, exactly what you will construct and how you will construct it. The wording must be clear, explicit, and complete so that any language model can fully understand and follow the instructions without ambiguity. If the technical description refers to re‑implementing an existing software, do not include or mention the original software’s name in the prompt. Do not add any role‑playing, personalization, or polite filler phrases (e.g., ‘You are a software developer’, ‘As an expert’, ‘Please kindly’). The prompt must remain strictly technical, objective, and instruction‑focused. Absolutely no simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, or fake content is allowed. You must require the full software with (all) file(s), in complete, unabridged, production‑ready code. Read it letter by letter, line by line, from beginning to end—you need to understand and remember every little detail! Always read and retain every single character of the provided text content in memory, ensuring no detail is overlooked.

entries.answer:
Below is a single, comprehensive rewrite prompt that converts the provided technical description into an explicit build specification. It preserves the described architecture, workflow, constraints, and implementation intent, while omitting the original software’s name as requested. The attached text describes an AInative deep research system built around hybrid retrieval, phased orchestration, multimodel routing, capacity reservation, and citationgrounded report generation, including concrete infrastructure patterns such as Kubernetes, Redis coordination, atomic quota reservation, phasebased execution, and adaptive refinement loops.[1]

 Rewritten prompt

Construct a complete, productionready deep research platform from scratch. Build the full system end to end, with all source files, infrastructure definitions, services, workers, APIs, schemas, orchestration logic, persistence layers, monitoring, tests, and deployment configuration included in complete, unabridged code. Do not use placeholders, mocks, toy logic, dummy services, or simulated outputs. Implement a real system that performs longhorizon research tasks reliably, supports multihour executions without losing task direction, and produces structured, citationgrounded final reports.[1]

Begin by implementing the system as a hybrid research infrastructure rather than a single monolithic languagemodel workflow. Build a retrieval layer that combines two categories of sources under one unified interface: first, internally hosted fulltext indexed corpora for large, frequently accessed domain collections; second, externally queried live APIs for timesensitive or specialized data feeds. The retrieval layer must expose a common query contract, normalized result schema, ranking pipeline, source attribution metadata, and document fetch interface. The internal indexing subsystem must support largescale fulltext corpora, periodic refresh pipelines, metadata extraction, chunking, embeddings or lexical retrieval where appropriate, and citationpreserving storage of original source references. The livesource connector layer must support external APIs for realtime, governmental, scientific, financial, environmental, and logisticsstyle feeds, with standardized adapters, retries, schema normalization, throttling, and source traceability.[1]

Next, implement execution infrastructure for large numbers of concurrent research jobs. The system must run as distributed task workloads across a containerized cluster, with each longrunning research task isolated in its own worker execution context. Use an orchestration model where many research jobs can run in parallel across a scalable container environment. Add a central coordination layer backed by Redis to track provider capacity, task state, queue priority, reservations, progress checkpoints, and interphase handoff state. Design this Redis layer to maintain perprovider and permodel capacity metrics, including requestperminute limits and tokenperminute limits for both input and output. Build atomic reservation logic so a task only proceeds when all required capacity reservations succeed together; otherwise, no reservation is applied. Implement these atomic checks with serverside scripts or equivalent transactional logic to guarantee allornothing quota booking under concurrency.[1]

Then build a phased orchestration engine for research execution. Do not design the system as one continuous prompt with evergrowing context. Instead, represent research as explicit phases with independent contexts, persisted state, and review gates between them. Implement at least the following phases: planning, research, synthesis, refinement, and final report generation. In the planning phase, parse the user’s question, infer subproblems, identify required source types, derive an initial research plan, and produce a structured research strategy artifact. In the research phase, execute parallel retrieval steps against internal indexes and external APIs, persist findings in a central research state, rank evidence, deduplicate results, and attach source metadata to every retained finding. In the synthesis phase, aggregate findings into coherent claims, identify contradictions, reconcile source disagreements, and draft evidencebacked conclusions. In the refinement phase, evaluate remaining knowledge gaps, missing source categories, unresolved conflicts, or weakly supported claims, and trigger additional research iterations when needed. In the final report phase, generate a structured output with all claims tied to citations and supporting sources.[1]

Implement explicit longhorizon task control so the system can operate for extended periods without drifting offtopic. Add a durable research strategy parameter to each job that records objectives, scope boundaries, key concepts, required evidence types, unresolved questions, and output expectations. Ensure every phase receives this strategy as a control artifact rather than relying on the model to infer the objective from prior freeform conversation alone. Persist this strategy externally so later phases and retries can resume accurately. Build discoverydriven redirection logic after each research iteration. After every batch of retrieval actions, evaluate what information is still missing, which source classes remain unexplored, whether any conflicts require targeted followup, and whether the system has converged sufficiently to proceed. Continue iterating only while unresolved information gaps remain and while the execution budget allows. The stopping condition must be information completeness and report quality, not arbitrary repetition.[1]

Add review gates between phases to prevent silent failure, drift, or infinite loops. After planning, validate whether the plan is relevant and complete enough to execute. After research, validate whether evidence coverage is sufficient and whether any critical source classes are missing. After synthesis, validate whether the draft is logically consistent, sufficiently grounded, and complete. If any review fails, route the task back to the appropriate upstream phase with explicit remediation instructions. Enforce configurable upper bounds on iterations, time budget, token budget, and retrieval steps per mode, while still allowing longrunning modes to extend substantially beyond shortform searches.[1]

Build multimodel orchestration instead of assuming a single model performs every task. Create provideragnostic model routing with ordered preference lists per phase. Allow a primary model, fallback model, and additional alternatives for each orchestration stage. Implement overflow handling so when a preferred model exceeds capacity thresholds, the task automatically falls through to the next eligible model. Add providerlevel circuit breakers so repeated failures or degraded upstream availability temporarily disable affected routes. When a route is unavailable, place tasks into a managed queue or reroute them according to policy rather than failing the entire research job immediately. Support graceful degradation, retries, and queue prioritization, including prioritizing jobs that are close to completion when capacity is constrained.[1]

Implement adaptive capacity forecasting rather than static worstcase allocation. Model token usage separately by phase because research and writing phases have different input/output token profiles. Track real consumption over time per task mode and per phase. Use percentilebased reservation estimates and arrivalrateaware forecasting to determine how much capacity to reserve. The reservation mechanism must reduce waste compared with static worstcase assumptions while still protecting the system from overcommitment. Persist telemetry about actual consumption and feed it back into reservation planning so the system improves over time.[1]

Create userfacing research modes with different ceilings for duration, step count, and cost profile. Each mode must map to distinct orchestration budgets, iteration ceilings, and modelselection policies. Longrunning modes must support approximately multihour execution windows and more iterative refinement than short modes. Ensure that all modes still use the same phased architecture and durable state management rather than separate codepaths.[1]

Build the output layer to generate structured research reports with citation grounding on every substantive claim. Every statement in the final report must be traceable to retrieved evidence. Support markdown output, structured machinereadable output, and persisted report artifacts. Store provenance for every finding, including source identifier, retrieval timestamp where applicable, normalization metadata, and any conflictresolution notes. Include attribution and source listings as firstclass report components rather than postprocessing decorations.[1]

Implement complete observability and reliability features. Add distributed tracing across orchestration phases, structured logs for all retrieval and model calls, metrics for latency, throughput, queue depth, failure rates, source coverage, token usage, and completion quality. Add dashboards and alerts for provider degradation, queue starvation, reservation contention, and abnormal retry loops. Build resumability so interrupted jobs can restart from persisted phase state instead of beginning from scratch.[1]

Deliver the system as a full production repository with complete code, deployment manifests, environment configuration templates, infrastructureascode, Redis scripts, worker services, API services, retrieval connectors, indexing pipelines, orchestration state machine, report generator, tests, and documentation. Do not mention or reference any existing branded implementation anywhere in the code, architecture description, prompts, comments, or documentation.[1]

 Notes

I kept the rewrite strictly technical, removed roleplay and filler, and omitted the original software’s name inside the rewritten prompt itself, while preserving the architecture and implementation requirements from the source text. If you want, I can next turn this into an even more executionoriented “master build prompt” with explicit repository structure, service boundaries, filebyfile deliverables, and required acceptance criteria.[1]
